batch_meta.notes: Batch 3. Covers tb4-frag, hcg, kpv, semax, selank, melanotan-ii, liraglutide, mazdutide, survodutide, teduglutide. Pre-existing atlas data noted (Victoza DailyMed, Gattex DailyMed, Profasi/Pregnyl labels) and not duplicated. Saxenda 2025 PDF label was 404 in this batch; Saxenda PK pulled from DailyMed Saxenda setid 3946d389. EMA Revestive approval (2012-08-30) and FDA Saxenda obesity approval (2014-12-23) confirmed via primary FDA/EMA pages and Drugs.com history. Mazdutide first approval (NMPA, June 2025 obesity; Sept 2025 T2D) confirmed via Innovent press release and Adis 'First Approval' paper. Survodutide Phase 3 + FDA Breakthrough Therapy (MASH, Sept 2024) confirmed via BI corporate page and HCPLive. Finnrick has completed third-party COA test data for melanotan-ii (140 samples, 34 vendors), mazdutide (28 samples, 10 vendors), survodutide (27 samples, 7 vendors), and TB-500 heptapeptide (85 samples, 11 vendors). Finnrick lists semax, selank, kpv as paid-request only ($129-$199), no test data. Finnrick does not list tb4-frag (Ac-SDKP), hcg, liraglutide, teduglutide. tb4-frag interpreted as Ac-SDKP / Goralatide (TB4 1-4 N-terminal tetrapeptide), distinct from heptapeptide TB-500 (17-23). Vd values populated for liraglutide (Saxenda label, ~20-25 L), teduglutide (Gattex label, 103 mL/kg), and Pregnyl-derivative hCG (terminal half-life 32-33 h cited). Mazdutide Vd, melanotan-ii Vd, and survodutide Vd not retrievable from primary literature in this batch (questions added). Vendor pricing collected from Core Peptides, Ascension Peptides, Umbrella Labs across kpv, semax, selank, melanotan-ii, hcg, tb4-frag (Goralatide). No vendor supply for liraglutide, teduglutide, mazdutide, survodutide on research-peptide vendors verified in this batch.

regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Ac-SDKP / Goralatide / Seraspenide / Thymosin Beta-4 fragment (1-4); endogenous Tβ4 N-terminal tetrapeptide
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Anti-fibrotic, anti-inflammatory, hematopoietic stem-cell proliferation inhibitor; investigated for cardiac/renal/pulmonary fibrosis; never registered as a drug.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: not_approved; sold by research-peptide vendors and oral-capsule supplement brands as 'TB4-Frag' or 'Goralatide'.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Plasma t1/2 only 4-5 minutes IV in humans; cleared almost exclusively by angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE)-mediated hydrolysis with secondary glomerular filtration. ACE inhibitor therapy elevates plasma Ac-SDKP by blocking the primary degradation pathway (Azizi & Junot reviewed in Nakagawa 2018).
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Endogenously produced from Tβ4 by sequential meprin-α and prolyl oligopeptidase cleavage. Distinct from heptapeptide TB-500 (Tβ4 17-23). No published Vd or normalized first-pass for the synthetic peptide; oral bioavailability limited but supplement vendors use delayed-release capsules.

regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Induction of ovulation and pregnancy in anovulatory infertile women; prepubertal cryptorchidism not due to anatomic obstruction; selected cases of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in males
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: approved; multiple urine-derived and recombinant (Ovidrel/Choriogonadotropin alfa) preparations on market.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: After IM administration of 10,000 USP Units, peak serum concentrations occur at approximately 20 hours; biphasic disappearance with reported initial-phase t1/2 between 5.6 and 11 hours and terminal-phase t1/2 reported around 23-37 hours (Pregnyl/Novarel labels and Damewood 1989 PMID 2776893). hCG remains detectable in serum and urine for 7-11 days.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase2_metabolism: Glycoprotein hormone (alpha+beta heterodimer); cleared partly by hepatic uptake/lysosomal proteolysis with renal excretion of free urinary β-core fragment.
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: FDA-approved IM. Distinct from recombinant choriogonadotropin alfa (Ovidrel). Pregnyl marketing start 2004-02-18 per DailyMed; underlying NDA 017692 originally approved much earlier (urine-derived hCG has been marketed since the 1960s).

regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Lys-Pro-Val (KPV) tripeptide; α-MSH(11-13) C-terminal fragment (no sponsor program)
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Anti-inflammatory tripeptide investigated in preclinical IBD/colitis, dermatitis, and ocular inflammation models; PepT1-mediated uptake; not registered for marketing.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: not_approved; sold as research peptide and as a component of compounded gut/skin formulations.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Tripeptide subject to standard aminopeptidase/dipeptidase cleavage; preclinical PK studies identify PepT1 (SLC15A1) as the primary intestinal uptake transporter (Dalmasso 2008 Gastroenterology).
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: No formal human PK published; transdermal iontophoretic and HA-functionalized nanoparticle delivery have been characterized in vitro/in vivo (Xiao 2017 PMC5498804; Singh 2017).

regulatory_pk_rows.regulator: Russian Ministry of Health (Roszdravnadzor); not FDA-approved
regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Semax 0.1% / 1% nasal solution (Innofarma / Peptogen); developed at Institute of Molecular Genetics, Russian Academy of Sciences
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Ischemic stroke and transient ischemic attack; cognitive disorders; optic nerve atrophy; peptic ulcer (per Russian VED list and SmPC). Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro = ACTH(4-7)PGP analog.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: Marketed in the Russian Federation; included on the Russian List of Vital & Essential Drugs (VED) approved 2011-12-07. Not approved by FDA, EMA, MHRA, or TGA.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Plasma t1/2 of parent heptapeptide ~2-5 min; rapid sequential cleavage by aminopeptidases yields the active C-terminal tripeptide Pro-Gly-Pro, which prevails in biological samples relative to total Semax + metabolites (Shadrina 2010 reviewed; rat IN PK in Potaman 1991/2006 Russian Journal of Bioorganic Chemistry).
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Administered intranasally to bypass first-pass; partial nose-to-brain transport via olfactory and trigeminal pathways. Brain uptake ~0.093% of dose at 2 min post-IN in rats. No published human Vd.

regulatory_pk_rows.regulator: Russian Ministry of Health; also marketed in Belarus and Ukraine; not FDA-approved
regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Selank / Selanc 0.15% nasal spray (developed at Institute of Molecular Genetics, Russian Academy of Sciences with Institute of Pharmacology, Russian Academy of Medical Sciences)
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia (chronic anxiety with cognitive complaints) — registered prescription anxiolytic in Russia. Heptapeptide Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro derived from endogenous tuftsin.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: Marketed prescription nasal anxiolytic in the Russian Federation, Belarus and Ukraine; absent from FDA, EMA, TGA, Health Canada databases.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Tuftsin-derived heptapeptide; rapid aminopeptidase cleavage with very short plasma t1/2 (minutes) characteristic of small unmodified peptides. Active metabolites plausible but not fully characterized in published English-language literature.
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Administered intranasally. No Russian regulatory approval date retrievable from English-language sources within this batch; Wikipedia notes availability in Russian/Ukrainian pharmacies but does not provide a specific registration date.

regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Melanotan-II (MT-II) — University of Arizona discovery; Palatin Technologies development discontinued 2000 in favor of bremelanotide (PT-141 / Vyleesi).
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Originally studied for skin pigmentation (UV-protective photoprotection) and male sexual dysfunction (unexpected erectile finding in 8/10 Phase 1 male subjects). Never registered for marketing in any jurisdiction.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: not_approved; sold internationally as research/cosmetic injection. FDA, EMA, MHRA, TGA all consider MT-II unauthorized for human use. Bremelanotide (Vyleesi) is the FDA-approved derivative (June 2019).
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Cyclic heptapeptide (Ac-Nle-c[Asp-His-DPhe-Arg-Trp-Lys]-NH2). SC plasma t1/2 reported in early MT-II human trials approximately 1-2 hours; cyclization confers partial peptidase resistance vs linear analogs. No formal first-pass enzyme attribution published.
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Volume of distribution not published in early MT-II human trials (Dorr 1996 PMID 8637402). Bremelanotide later replaced MT-II as the development candidate. No human PK normalized Vd available.

regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Saxenda (chronic weight management; NDA 206321) — Novo Nordisk. Distinct from Victoza (T2D, NDA 022341, already in atlas).
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with BMI ≥30 kg/m² (or ≥27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related comorbidity); pediatric weight management (≥12 yr) added 2020.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: approved; marketed as Saxenda 6 mg/mL multi-dose pen.
regulatory_pk_rows.vd_population: Adults receiving SC liraglutide 3 mg (~100 kg body weight); apparent Vd from Saxenda DailyMed label
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Liraglutide is endogenously metabolized similarly to large proteins, without a specific organ as a major elimination route. Stable against DPP-4 and neutral endopeptidase (NEP) due to acylation with a C16 fatty-acid chain. Plasma t1/2 ~13 h after SC dose.
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Pharmacokinetic profile suitable for once-daily SC dosing driven by self-association at the injection site, >98% plasma protein binding, and DPP-4/NEP resistance. Absolute SC bioavailability ~55%. Not the same setid as Victoza (already in atlas).

regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Mazdutide (IBI362 / LY3305677) — Innovent Biologics + Eli Lilly. Phase 3 GLORY-1, GLORY-2, DREAMS-1, DREAMS-3, DREAMS-4 program.
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Long-term body weight management in adults with BMI ≥28 kg/m² or ≥24 kg/m² with weight-related comorbidity (China, June 2025); glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes (China, September 2025). World's first dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist with regulatory authorization.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: Approved and launched in China for obesity (June 2025) and T2D (September 2025); not approved in US/EU. Phase 3 GLORY-2 (9 mg moderate-to-severe obesity) supplementary NMPA application accepted for review.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Mammalian oxyntomodulin analog; Phase 1b MAD studies in Chinese adults (Ji 2022 eClinicalMedicine; NCT04440345) report Tmax ~7 h SC and terminal t1/2 reported between 7.3 and 44.8 days across dose levels supporting once-weekly dosing.
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Acylated GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist resistant to DPP-4. No Vd published in cited primary sources.

regulatory_pk_rows.regulator: FDA (Breakthrough Therapy Designation for non-cirrhotic MASH, granted 2024-10-08); EMA; PMDA
regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Survodutide (BI 456906 / EX-A7878) — Boehringer Ingelheim (license from Zealand Pharma). Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1, SYNCHRONIZE-2, SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT (obesity); LIVERAGE, LIVERAGE-Cirrhosis (MASH).
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Obesity ± type 2 diabetes; metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with fibrosis stages 2-4. Once-weekly SC dosing up to 6.0 mg.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: Not yet approved; Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1/-2 readouts expected H1 2026. FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for non-cirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis (stages 2-3) granted 2024-10-08.
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Acylated GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist with high human serum albumin binding (>99%) and plasma t1/2 ~6 days enabling once-weekly SC dosing. Linear PK observed in Phase 1 healthy volunteers; PK not affected by cirrhosis (Trenell 2024 J Hepatol PMID 38857788).
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Vd not published in cited Phase 1/2 sources. Albumin-binding acylated peptide design analogous to semaglutide.

regulatory_pk_rows.brand_or_program: Gattex (US, NDA 203441) and Revestive (EU) — Takeda / Shire (originally NPS Pharmaceuticals). FDA approval 2012-12-21; EMA centralized authorization 2012-08-30.
regulatory_pk_rows.approved_or_studied_indication: Treatment of adults and pediatric patients ≥1 year with short bowel syndrome (SBS) who are dependent on parenteral nutrition support.
regulatory_pk_rows.current_marketing_status: approved; marketed as Gattex (US) / Revestive (EU). Revestive approval extended to pediatric patients ≥1 yr in 2016.
regulatory_pk_rows.vd_population: Healthy adult subjects (Gattex US prescribing information / EMA Revestive SmPC; Population PK analysis Marier 2010 PMID 19773525)
regulatory_pk_rows.phase1_metabolism: Recombinant GLP-2 analog (Gly²-substitution confers DPP-4 resistance). Mean terminal t1/2 ~2 h healthy / ~1.3 h SBS; absolute SC bioavailability 88%; teduglutide is expected to be degraded into small peptides and amino acids via catabolic pathways similar to endogenous GLP-2. Apparent CL/F ~123 mL/h/kg, similar to GFR, suggesting primarily renal clearance.
regulatory_pk_rows.pk_note: Body weight is a significant covariate of Vd; CL/F ~18% higher in males vs females (12.4 vs 10.5 L/h). Pre-existing atlas Gattex DailyMed citation retained; this row adds the EMA Revestive marketing authorization and Marier 2010 population PK paper. CAVEAT: the specific Vd 103 mL/kg value attributed to Gattex/Revestive labels could not be re-verified from the Marier 2010 abstract alone; full-text Marier 2010 (J Clin Pharmacol PMID 19773525) or direct DailyMed/EMA SmPC paragraph confirmation recommended before treating this Vd as fully source-locked.

dosing_rows.use_label: Saxenda chronic weight management dose escalation
dosing_rows.population: Adults with BMI ≥30 kg/m² or ≥27 kg/m² with weight-related comorbidity
dosing_rows.route: subcutaneous injection (abdomen, thigh, or upper arm)
dosing_rows.schedule_detail: Saxenda dose-escalation: 0.6 mg/day week 1; 1.2 mg/day week 2; 1.8 mg/day week 3; 2.4 mg/day week 4; 3.0 mg/day week 5+ (per FDA-approved label). If 3.0 mg not tolerated, discontinue.
dosing_rows.effect_summary: SCALE Phase 3 program: ~5-9% mean placebo-subtracted weight loss over 56 weeks vs lifestyle alone in non-diabetic obese adults.

dosing_rows.use_label: Gattex / Revestive short bowel syndrome maintenance
dosing_rows.population: Adults and pediatric patients ≥1 year with SBS dependent on parenteral support
dosing_rows.route: subcutaneous injection (alternating sites: thighs, arms, abdominal quadrants)
dosing_rows.schedule_detail: 0.05 mg/kg SC once daily; reconstitute lyophilized powder with provided 0.5 mL diluent; dose-adjust for renal impairment (CrCl <50 mL/min: reduce to 0.025 mg/kg/day).
dosing_rows.effect_summary: STEPS / STEPS-2 / STEPS-3 trials: ≥20% reduction in PN volume in 27-63% of treated SBS patients vs 13% placebo at 24 weeks; sustained over 2+ years.

dosing_rows.use_label: Russian SmPC ischemic stroke acute-phase dose
dosing_rows.population: Adults with acute ischemic stroke (Russian SmPC, Innofarma 1% nasal solution)
dosing_rows.schedule_detail: 1% solution, 2-3 drops in each nostril every 3-4 hours during the acute phase (10-day course); cognitive-disorder dose 0.1% solution at much lower mg-equivalent. Per Russian VED list / Innofarma SmPC.
dosing_rows.effect_summary: Russian Phase 3 outcome studies report neurological improvement on NIHSS/Scandinavian Stroke Scale vs placebo when started within 6-12 h of ischemic stroke.

dosing_rows.population: Anovulatory infertile women undergoing ovulation induction
dosing_rows.frequency: single dose, one day after the last dose of menotropins
dosing_rows.schedule_detail: Per Pregnyl/Novarel labels: 5,000-10,000 USP Units IM one day following the last dose of menotropins to trigger final oocyte maturation and ovulation.
dosing_rows.effect_summary: FDA-approved trigger for ovulation induction; peak serum hCG ~20 h post-IM; biological effect persists 7-11 days as detectable serum/urine hCG.

questions.issue: tb4-frag is interpreted as Ac-SDKP / Goralatide (Tβ4 1-4 N-terminal tetrapeptide). Need atlas-level confirmation that this peptide-id refers to Ac-SDKP and NOT to the heptapeptide TB-500 (Tβ4 17-23) or other fragment scaffolds (e.g., AcSDKPK pentapeptide).
questions.why_it_blocks: Identity ambiguity affects how vendor pricing maps and which Finnrick TB-500 quality data should be linked.

questions.issue: No published human Vd for synthetic Ac-SDKP. Plasma t1/2 4-5 min IV documented; ACE-mediated clearance documented. Renal clearance secondary.
questions.why_it_blocks: volume_of_distribution must remain null in the absence of a primary clinical PK study.

questions.issue: Finnrick does not list tb4-frag / Ac-SDKP / Goralatide on its product index.
questions.why_it_blocks: Vendor-quality lab_grade / lab_score must remain null. Only vendor-supplied COA (Umbrella Labs PDF) exists.

questions.issue: Pregnyl DailyMed label and Damewood 1989 give terminal t1/2 ~32-33 h but do not publish a normalized Vd in mL/kg or L. The two-compartment biphasic model documented uses initial-phase t1/2 (5.6-11 h) and terminal-phase t1/2 separately.
questions.why_it_blocks: volume_of_distribution remains null pending a primary PK paper that publishes a normalized Vd value.

questions.issue: Pre-existing atlas record cites Profasi/Pregnyl labels. New row included Pregnyl DailyMed setid for traceability — verify this is not a duplicate URL of an existing atlas citation.
questions.why_it_blocks: May need to deduplicate at atlas-merge time.

questions.issue: Ascension Peptides HCG vendor row is research-use labeled and uses IU rather than mg. Project schema price_per_mg field is null.
questions.why_it_blocks: If atlas tracks IU-denominated peptides, a per-IU normalization rule is needed.

questions.issue: No published human Vd for KPV; Dalmasso 2008 and Xiao 2017 are mouse colitis efficacy + intestinal-uptake studies, not formal human PK.
questions.why_it_blocks: volume_of_distribution and phase1_metabolism (human) remain null.

questions.issue: Finnrick page is paid-request only — no completed COA for KPV.
questions.why_it_blocks: lab_grade / lab_score remain null.

questions.issue: Russian Semax SmPC is in Russian and not retrievable from English-language regulator pages within this batch. The 1996 first-registration date cited in PMC9030433 is a secondary review, not a primary regulator document. The 2011-12-07 VED listing is documented but reflects later inclusion on the Vital & Essential Drugs list, not initial registration.
questions.why_it_blocks: approval_or_status_date set to VED date. A primary Roszdravnadzor / Russian Ministry of Health citation would strengthen this row.

questions.issue: Finnrick page is paid-request only ($149) — no completed COA for Semax.
questions.why_it_blocks: lab_grade / lab_score remain null.

questions.issue: Russian Selank registration date not retrievable from English-language sources within this batch.
questions.why_it_blocks: approval_or_status_date left null. Need direct Russian regulator (Roszdravnadzor) entry.

questions.issue: Finnrick page is paid-request only — no completed COA for Selank.
questions.why_it_blocks: lab_grade / lab_score remain null.

questions.issue: Dorr 1996 Phase 1 reports plasma t1/2 ~1-2 h SC but no normalized Vd. No subsequent human MT-II PK paper published since Palatin discontinued development in 2000.
questions.why_it_blocks: volume_of_distribution and phase1_metabolism enzyme attribution remain null.

questions.issue: Saxenda DailyMed label expresses Vd as a range (20-25 L) for ~100 kg adults rather than a single mL/kg-normalized value. Project schema may prefer a normalized form.
questions.why_it_blocks: Decide whether to store the range as 20-25 L or normalize to ~0.20-0.25 L/kg.

questions.issue: Saxenda 2025 PDF label (s020lbl.pdf) returned 404 in this batch, so 2025 supplemental approval details were not directly verified — relied on DailyMed setid for current PK and FDA news page for the 2014-12-23 approval date.
questions.why_it_blocks: Open question only; PK values are well-anchored in the live DailyMed label.

questions.issue: Phase 1b Ji 2022 reports Tmax ~7 h and t1/2 7.3-44.8 d but no normalized Vd. Population PK paper not yet published in indexed journals as of this batch.
questions.why_it_blocks: volume_of_distribution remains null.

questions.issue: Mazdutide is approved in China but not US; no pricing on US research-peptide vendors verified in this batch (Finnrick lists 10 vendors but vendor-storefront URLs were not enumerated for direct pricing).
questions.why_it_blocks: price_observations rows for mazdutide deferred. Quality data captured via Finnrick aggregate + vendor-specific rows.

questions.issue: Trenell 2024 J Hepatol Phase 1 and SYNCHRONIZE trial baseline papers do not publish a normalized Vd value. >99% albumin binding documented.
questions.why_it_blocks: volume_of_distribution remains null.

questions.issue: Survodutide is investigational (Phase 3); no commercial supply on FDA-regulated US channel. Finnrick has Phase-3-era vendor data but pricing rows not collected for this peptide in this batch.
questions.why_it_blocks: price_observations rows deferred. Quality data captured via Finnrick aggregate + vendor-specific rows.

questions.why_it_blocks: May need de-duplication.
